panels.description: The overall cluster state — normally RUNNING. INITIALIZING means it is still starting up, PAUSED means it has stopped accepting most client work, and SHUTTINGDOWN means it is stopping. Watch this to confirm the cluster is healthy and available.
panels.title: State

panels.description: Whether the cluster still has its full data redundancy. FULL means every partition has all of its configured copies; REDUCED means one or more copies are missing (for example after a node failure), so the cluster is running with less resilience until it recovers.
panels.title: Safety
Current size
panels.description: The number of nodes currently live in the cluster. Compare it with the normal (configured) size to see whether nodes have been lost or added.

panels.title: Normal size
panels.description: The number of nodes the cluster is configured to run with. If the current size is below this, the cluster is missing nodes.

panels.title: Sites/host
panels.description: The number of parallel execution sites configured on each node. Together with the node count, this determines how much work the cluster can run in parallel.

panels.title: Uptime
panels.description: How long the cluster has been running since it last started. An unexpected reset here indicates a restart.

panels.title: Nodes
panels.description: A per-node summary of the cluster: each node's host name, VoltDB version, current CPU load, uptime, and whether it is ready for cross-datacenter replication (XDCR). Use it to spot nodes that are overloaded, on the wrong version, or recently restarted.

panels.title: Max CPU
panels.description: The CPU usage of the busiest node, as a percentage. This measures the VoltDB server process only, not everything else running on the machine. A sustained high value is a signal that the cluster may need to scale out.

panels.title: RAM usage
panels.description: The share of physical memory used by the VoltDB process on the busiest node, from 0 to 1. Rising memory is a signal that the cluster may be approaching its capacity.

panels.title: Java heap
panels.description: The share of the configured maximum Java heap in use on the busiest node, from 0 to 1. A value close to 1 means the heap is nearly full, which can cause pauses or instability.

The rate of transactions the cluster is executing per second, counted once per client request - the fan-out to partition replicas in a K-safe cluster is not double-counted. It is the main measure of how much load the cluster is handling.
panels.title: Transactions/s
GC time
panels.description: Total time the Java garbage collector spent pausing work over the selected time range. Large or growing values point to memory pressure that can slow the cluster down.

panels.title: Volt Version
panels.description: The VoltDB software version the cluster is running. Use it to confirm the expected version and to catch a node left behind during an upgrade.

panels.title: CPU Usage
panels.description: CPU usage of each node over time, as a percentage. This reflects the VoltDB server process only, not the whole machine. Use it to see how load is spread across nodes and whether any node is running hot.

panels.title: Transaction rate
panels.description: The rate of client transactions each node is handling per second, counted once per request without the replica fan-out. Use it to watch throughput trends and see whether work is balanced evenly across nodes.

panels.title: RSS size
panels.description: The total memory held by the VoltDB process on each node over time. Watch for steady growth, which can indicate the cluster is filling up its available memory.

panels.title: IdleTime
panels.description: Accumulated time each node's execution sites have spent waiting for new work. The faster this line rises, the more idle the node is: a steep climb suggests the cluster is underused and could scale down, while a nearly flat line means the sites are kept busy and the cluster is near capacity.

A history of recent partition-rebalancing operations, which run when the cluster changes size and data is redistributed across nodes. Rebalancing proceeds in segments, so the 'average' columns are averages across those segments. Use it to track progress and how long a resize is taking.
panels.title: Recent rebalances
